summary: Tom Scott describes trying ChatGPT to fix his Gmail labels and being unsettled by how capable it was. He argues that we cannot know where we are on the technology curve, comparing it to Napster.
why_hn: HN cites it for the argument that we cannot tell whether AI is early or late on its sigmoid curve until hindsight.

title: Jordan Peterson - Controversial Facts about IQ
summary: A clip of psychologist Jordan Peterson lecturing on intelligence and IQ, covering how it is defined and its correlation with academic and work success.
why_hn: HN commenters use it as supporting material in arguments about IQ and the g-factor view of intelligence.

title: What I Wish I Had Known Before Scaling Uber to 1000 Services • Matt Ranney • GOTO 2016
summary: Matt Ranney of Uber talks at GOTO Chicago 2016 about what Uber learned from growing past 1,000 production microservices. He covers regrets, sprawl and organizational effects.
why_hn: Often brought up as an honest account of microservice sprawl, including the fact that nobody at Uber knew exactly how many services existed.

title: Joscha: From Computation to Consciousness (31c3)
summary: Joscha Bach's 31c3 talk argues that the mind should be understood as an information-processing system and that even the physical universe can be seen as computational. It tours the philosophy underlying artificial intelligence and cognitive science.
why_hn: HN recommends it as an inspiring summary of a computational model of mind and a first lecture in a series on the brain as a computer.

title: There is No Algorithm for Truth - with Tom Scott
summary: Tom Scott's Royal Institution discourse on science communication in the age of social media, how recommendation algorithms shape popularity, and why view counts can matter more than truth. It includes a segment on parasocial relationships.
why_hn: HN returns to it in discussions of algorithmic feeds, misinformation and parasocial relationships, as a clear and thoughtful talk.

title: The Hyperbolic Geometry of DMT Experiences (@Harvard Science of Psychedelics Club)
summary: Andres Gomez Emilsson of the Qualia Research Institute presents a model of DMT experiences using hyperbolic geometry and dynamical systems theory. He describes how different intoxication levels correspond to changing curvature and information content of experience.
why_hn: HN commenters point to it as an interesting lecture related to psychedelics, brain geometry and hyperbolic space, with a good intro to hyperbolic geometry.

title: Speaking Piano - Now with (somewhat decent) captions!
summary: A player piano is made to reproduce human speech, here reciting a European Environmental Criminal Court proclamation in German at the 2009 World Venice Forum. This upload adds subtitles so the words become understandable.
why_hn: HN recommends it as the canonical talking-piano example, uncanny and impressive once you read the captions.

title: Carbon Capture Isn't Real
summary: Adam Something gives a short, sarcastic argument that carbon capture does not live up to its promises. He says the energy it uses would be better spent replacing fossil sources directly.
why_hn: HN commenters cite it to argue carbon capture is a distraction from stopping emissions at the source.

title: Tea Consent
summary: A three-minute animated video that explains sexual consent through the analogy of offering someone a cup of tea. It is based on a blog post by Emmeline May.
why_hn: Used as the classic analogy for consent, applied to opt-out data collection and privacy practices.

title: Roger Penrose: Physics of Consciousness and the Infinite Universe | Lex Fridman Podcast #85
summary: Lex Fridman interviews physicist Roger Penrose on consciousness, the limits of computation, quantum mechanics and his cyclic cosmology. It covers his views on AI and the big bang.
why_hn: HN recommends it as an accessible walkthrough of Penrose's ideas on consciousness and cosmology, interesting even if debatable.

title: Chris Lattner: Future of Programming and AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #381
summary: Lex Fridman's long podcast conversation with Chris Lattner, creator of Swift, LLVM and MLIR and co-founder of Modular. Topics include the Mojo language, the future of programming and AI, and hardware.
why_hn: HN points to it as the main place to hear Lattner's motivations and design ideas for Mojo, often in Mojo threads.

title: Was Roman Concrete Better?
summary: Practical Engineering compares modern concrete with that of the Roman Empire, covering modern techniques like roller compacted concrete and water-reducing admixtures. It explains the tradeoffs of Roman construction versus reinforced concrete.
why_hn: HN recommends it as a clear, balanced answer to claims that Roman concrete was better than ours.

title: The UK Election Results Were the Worst in History
summary: CGP Grey explains how the 2015 UK general election showed the flaws of first-past-the-post voting, with parties like UKIP winning many votes but few seats.
why_hn: HN recommends it as a short, clear illustration of how first-past-the-post misrepresents voters.

title: Gridfinity: Your Ultimate Modular Workshop is FREE!
summary: Zack Freedman introduces Gridfinity, his free, open-source modular workshop storage system of 3D-printable bins and baseplates. The video walks through the design, the parametric templates and the many module types that fit parts, tools and accessories.
why_hn: HN points people to it as the original explanation of what Gridfinity is and why it exists, in threads about the project and its catalogs.

title: Farbrausch & Neuro - Masagin (HD Stereo)
summary: Masagin is a realtime demoscene production by Farbrausch and Neuro with music by paniq, using animated recursive SVG graphics made in Inkscape. It is a psychedelic, nested-dials audiovisual piece.
why_hn: HN recommends it as a showcase of what the demoscene can do, with high-res antialiased vector graphics and motion blur.

title: How to Age Gracefully | CBC Radio
summary: A five-minute CBC Radio WireTap farewell video in which people of all ages offer words of wisdom to younger people. The advice is short and funny, and keeps coming back to the point that nobody really knows what they are doing.
why_hn: Commenters bring it up in threads about life advice and aging as the best advice they have heard, namely to ignore advice and do your own thing.

title: Yanis Varoufakis with Professor Noam Chomsky at NYPL, April 16, 2016 | DiEM25
summary: Yanis Varoufakis and Noam Chomsky talk on stage at the New York Public Library in 2016. They cover the Greek financial crisis, European politics, neoliberalism and America's economic future, drawing on Varoufakis's book.
why_hn: Recommended as a long, insightful conversation that gives a view of how Greece was pressured during the bailouts.

title: Simon Peyton Jones - Linear Haskell: practical linearity in a higher-order polymorphic language
summary: Simon Peyton Jones presents linear types for Haskell, showing how practical linearity can fit into a higher-order polymorphic language. The talk covers motivations such as resource handling and relates the ideas to Rust.
why_hn: HN recommends it as a clear introduction to linear types in GHC from the language's lead designer.

title: Noam Chomsky - Manufacturing Consent
summary: A nine-minute excerpt from the 1992 documentary Manufacturing Consent in which Noam Chomsky summarizes how corporate media shapes public discourse.
why_hn: Cited as a short overview of the propaganda model whenever commenters discuss media influence and consent manufacturing.

title: Deadly Truth of General AI? - Computerphile
summary: A Computerphile video in which Rob Miles warns against assuming a general AI will think like a human. He uses the thought experiment of a stamp-collecting AI to show how a goal-driven system could pursue its aim with dangerous results.
why_hn: Often pointed to as an accessible first introduction to AI safety and why a superintelligent AI could be dangerous.
